summary_md:
**Revision 24 (D219): P2 now says which figures are sums.** A sum figure's lines total it (M2, M17, M18, M19-M25, monthly money in and trading receipts); an outflow figure (M8, M11, M12, M14, monthly money out) is shown positive and its lines total it negated; a derived figure (M9, averages, shares, ratios, counts, lowest balance, monthly balance and overdrawn-day cells) cites what it reads and is not asked to total.
M9 gains an evidence note naming, by id, the lines it counts only in part (a returned transfer capped at what was sent); it stays out of the method sentence and the prompt (R30).
R1, R11 and R16 change only where they cite P2; three new terms; no figure's value, sign or evidence changes, so T04's two P2 majors are answered and its R1, R2, R3 and P1 majors stand.
Context takes in T03's pass and merge, T12 blocked at 04ff28a (D217 pending), T17's first fail and T04's two fails; D211 and D212 are recorded in Options considered.
One question: is the monthly money-out cell a positive outflow like M8 (default) or a negative signed sum?

questions.context: Revision 24 (D219) says which figures are sums. D219 says that every monthly cell is a sum figure with signed evidence totalling it, and also that every figure the memo shows as money paid out is an outflow figure: a positive amount whose lines' signed amounts total it negated, as M8, M11, M12 and M14 are. R11's monthly cells include money out, and three cells that add no lines up (average and lowest end-of-day balance, days overdrawn), which revision 24 makes derived figures whatever you answer. The design makes the money-out cell an outflow figure: a monthly table then shows money out beside money in as a positive amount, as a bank statement's paid-out column does, with the same sign rule as M8 to M14. The alternative shows it as a negative amount that its lines total, so every flow cell totals its lines with no sign rule, but the money-out column is negative while M8 to M14 are positive. T06, which builds the monthly summary, has not started, so neither costs anything yet.
options: Money out as an outflow figure: a positive amount whose lines total it negated, like M8 (design default)
Money out as a signed sum: a negative amount that its lines total

requirements.md.old: The case log, once checked, shows whether the save's entry is among the recorded entries.
requirements.md.new: The case log, once checked, shows whether the save's entry is among the recorded entries. *Sum figure* (revision 24): a figure whose value is the total of its evidence lines' signed amounts: every money-in bucket, trading receipts (M2) among them, total money in (M17), cash deposits within trading receipts (M18), and each monthly money-in and trading-receipts cell. *Outflow figure* (revision 24): a figure that reports money paid out as a positive amount, whose evidence lines' signed amounts total the figure negated: debt service (M8), owner drawings (M11), VAT paid (M12), PAYE paid (M14), each monthly money-out cell, and every other figure the memo shows as money paid out. *Derived figure* (revision 24): every figure that is neither, net operating cash flow (M9), averages, shares, ratios, counts and a lowest balance among them, and each monthly balance and overdrawn-day cell. Its evidence is every line its calculation reads: for a lowest balance the line that set it, for an average end-of-day balance the lines that set each day's close (R12), and for net operating cash flow every line it adds or offsets. Its value is not the total of their amounts.

requirements.md.old: and SHALL report total money in and each bucket as a GBP figure with the ids of the lines behind it.
requirements.md.new: and SHALL report total money in and each bucket as a GBP figure with the ids of the lines behind it, each a sum figure whose lines' signed amounts total it to the penny (P2).

requirements.md.old: lowest end-of-day balance and days overdrawn, each cell with the ids of the lines behind it.
requirements.md.new: lowest end-of-day balance and days overdrawn, each cell with the ids of the lines behind it. The money-in and trading-receipts cells are sum figures, the money-out cell is an outflow figure, and the average and lowest end-of-day balance and days-overdrawn cells are derived figures (P2).

requirements.md.old: for a sum it SHALL show the lines' total next to the figure, and for an average, share, ratio or count it SHALL show the inputs and the method.
requirements.md.new: for a sum figure it SHALL show the total of the lines' signed amounts next to the figure, and for an outflow figure that total, saying that it is the figure negated; for a derived figure (an average, share, ratio, count or lowest balance, or net operating cash flow) it SHALL show the inputs and the method, and for net operating cash flow also the lines it counts only in part (P2).

requirements.md.old: For any sum figure, bucket or monthly cell, the signed amounts of its evidence lines SHALL total the figure to the penny.
requirements.md.new: For any sum figure, the signed amounts of its evidence lines SHALL total the figure to the penny; every money-in bucket, total money in (M17), cash deposits within trading receipts (M18), and each monthly money-in and trading-receipts cell is a sum figure. For any outflow figure, which is reported as a positive amount, the signed amounts of its evidence lines SHALL total the figure negated, to the penny; debt service (M8), owner drawings (M11), VAT paid (M12), PAYE paid (M14), each monthly money-out cell and every other figure the memo shows as money paid out is an outflow figure. A derived figure, such as net operating cash flow (M9), an average, share, ratio, count or lowest balance, or a monthly balance or overdrawn-day cell, is not a sum figure: its evidence is every line its calculation reads, and this property does not ask their amounts to total it. Net operating cash flow (M9) SHALL name, in a note carried with its evidence, each of its evidence lines that counts only in part: a credit from someone the business paid by transfer, which offsets no more than was sent to them.

**What T04's first two reviews showed, and what the owner decided** (verify-127, verify-128; D219, 2026-11-20)
- T04 builds the figures layer for R1, R2, R3, R7, P1, P2 and P6: M17, the money-in buckets, M18 and M26. Both reviews failed P2 on the same two majors, and neither is a fault of the build:

  - M9 cites in full a credit from someone the business paid by transfer, and counts it only up to what was sent to them (src/cma/metrics.py:300-302). With £100 sent and £150 sent back, M9 is £0 and its two lines total £50.

T04 has one attempt left.
- D219: clarify P2, and R1, R11 and R16 where they cite it. A sum figure is one whose value is the total of its lines' amounts. An outflow figure (M8, M11, M12, M14 and every other figure the memo shows as money paid out) is reported as a positive amount, and the signed amounts of its lines total it negated, to the penny. A derived figure (M9, ratios, averages, counts) is not a sum figure: its evidence is every line its calculation reads, P2 does not ask those lines to total it, and M9 says in its evidence note which lines count only in part. Every money-in bucket, M17, M18 and every monthly cell is a sum figure. Keep everything else in revision 23. Revision 24 writes it.

  - 'Every monthly cell'. R11's average and lowest end-of-day balance and days-overdrawn cells add no lines up, so no lines can total them. Revision 24 reads 'every monthly cell' as the cells that do: money in, money out and trading receipts. The money-out cell shows money paid out, which D219 makes an outflow figure, so revision 24 makes it one and asks the owner (Options considered).
  - 'Every line its calculation reads'. For a lowest balance (M5), the line that set it, and for an average end-of-day balance (M27), the lines that set each day's close, as M5 cites today and R12 asks. Read as every balance the calculation compares, M5 would cite every line of the statement, which helps no one check it. No figure's evidence changes.
  - 'Its evidence note'. M9's method sentence is shown in the prompt's metrics table and in the memo's appendix (src/cma/metrics.py:453 and src/cma/graph.py:170 at d7ec35f), and R30 keeps line-level data out of a prompt. So the note sits beside M9's evidence ids, in the evidence record and MCP, and names lines by id only.
- The lesson is D108's, for figures: a property about 'any sum figure' has to say which figures are sums, or a reviewer reads every GBP figure as one.

**Sub-decision: what P2 asks of each kind of figure (revision 24, after verify-127 and verify-128; D219).** P2 said that the signed amounts of a sum figure's lines total it, and named no sums. Read as every GBP figure, it failed M8, M11, M12 and M14, which report money paid out as positive amounts, and M9, which counts a returned transfer only up to what was sent. (i) Make every GBP figure a sum: report M8, M11, M12 and M14 as negative amounts, and cite for M9 only the lines that count in full. That changes four of M1-M16's values, which R10 forbids; the packaged policy compares M8 and M11 as positive amounts, and signed memos cite them so. A line is in M9's evidence wholly or not at all, so a capped credit would leave M9's evidence, hiding the line a person should look at. (ii) Three kinds. A sum figure's lines total it. An outflow figure is reported as a positive amount and its lines total it negated. A derived figure cites every line its calculation reads and is not asked to total them, and M9 names in an evidence note the lines it counts only in part. (iii) Keep P2's words and let each build say which figures are sums: each review would read 'sum' afresh, as verify-127 and verify-128 did. *Chose (ii)*, the owner's answer (D219), which P2, R1, R11 and R16 say since revision 24. What (ii) costs: a person checking an outflow by hand negates its lines' total, which the drill-down shows and names (R16), and M9 cannot be checked by adding its lines; its method and its note say what counts. *The monthly money-out cell:* (a) an outflow figure, a positive amount whose lines total it negated, like M8 (design default); (b) a signed sum, a negative amount its lines total, as D219's 'every monthly cell is a sum figure' reads on its own. (a) because a monthly table shows money out beside money in as a positive amount, as a bank statement's paid-out column does, and D219 makes every figure shown as money paid out an outflow figure. (b) would have every flow cell total its lines with no sign rule, at the cost of a money-out column that is negative while M8 to M14 are positive. Either way the balance and overdrawn-day cells are derived. Revision 24 asks the owner; T06, which builds the monthly summary, has not started.
